correctness.rationale: The cyclic-gap necessary-and-sufficient criterion gives the sharp universal upper bound n<=2t+3 floor(t/2), each residue witness and exact equality gap patterns. Complete replacement analysis gives only frozen configurations at n=7k (k>=2) and edges ±7 at n=7k+2. Full brute force for n=7..23 enumerates all smaller and minimum subsets, checks the independent neighborhood and gap tests, and reproduces the exchange graphs; no finite testing is used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural monitoring problem on the graph square of a cycle is governed by seven rather than five positions per minimal sensor block, correcting an explicit published numerical prediction. Despite seven optima at 7k being known, those optima become completely isolated when k>=2; adding two vertices produces a connected n-cycle of optima. This is a sharp structure-versus-count reconfiguration phenomenon across an infinite canonical family.
